title: Corrupted system files
symptom: Windows features fail with odd errors that suggest damaged system files
user_description: The Start menu won't open half the time and Settings closes on its own. Someone said my Windows files might be corrupt. Can you fix it without wiping everything?

options.why: Office is not the problem. The errors are in Windows itself.

options.text: Delete the damaged-looking files from System32
options.why: Deleting system files can stop Windows starting at all.
Registry cleaners do not repair system files and can cause new problems.

options.text: In an admin Command Prompt, run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, then sfc /scannow, then restart
options.why: DISM repairs the Windows image that SFC uses as its source, then SFC checks and replaces damaged system files.

hints: Does Windows have built-in tools to check its own files?
Do these tools need extra permissions?
Why might the order of the two tools matter?
real_world_tip: SFC writes a log you can check if it says it could not fix everything. Restart after the scans finish before you test again.
